result.overall: The court allowed the Minister's application for judicial review, finding the Board member erred in granting an extension of time for appeal without proper reasons or consideration of prejudice.

themes.name: Extension of Time Criteria
themes.summary: The court focused on the criteria for granting an extension of time for appeal under the CPP and analogous Federal Courts Act provisions.

themes.name: Respondent's Delay Explanation
themes.summary: The Respondent's reasons for delay were inconsistent and unsupported, undermining the justification for the extension.

themes.name: Prejudice to Minister
themes.summary: The court emphasized the need to consider prejudice to the Minister when granting extensions, which was not done here.

themes.name: Procedural Fairness and Ex Parte Decision
themes.summary: The decision was made ex parte without notice to the Minister, raising concerns about fairness and proper procedure.

arguments.claim: Respondent requested extension of time and leave to appeal despite delay due to personal difficulties.
arguments.quote: Ms. Gattellaro did not act earlier on this due to many difficulties in her life.

arguments.claim: Granted extension of time and leave to appeal seven and a half years late without reasons or Minister's submissions.
arguments.quote: the time within which to appeal was extended and the leave to appeal was granted. No reasons were provided.

arguments.claim: The Board member erred in granting extension of time and leave to appeal without proper consideration of criteria.
arguments.quote: the member erred in extending the time for bringing the appeal.

arguments.claim: The extension of time should not be granted as a matter of right and must consider prejudice to the Minister.
arguments.quote: The authority to extend the statutory limitation must not, in my view, be exercised arbitrarily or capriciously.

holdings.statement: The Board member erred in granting an extension of time for appeal without proper reasons and consideration of prejudice.
holdings.quote: the member erred in extending the time for bringing the appeal

holdings.statement: Criteria for granting extension of time include continuing intention to pursue appeal, arguable case, reasonable explanation for delay, and no prejudice to other party.
holdings.quote: the following criteria must be considered and weighed

holdings.statement: The Board's decision to extend time is discretionary but must not be arbitrary or capricious and should be principled.
holdings.quote: The authority to extend the statutory limitation must not, in my view, be exercised arbitrarily or capriciously.

holdings.statement: The decision is set aside and referred back to the Board for re-determination by a different member applying the proper criteria.
holdings.quote: The decision under review will be set aside and the matter referred back to the Board for re-determination

rebuttals.point: Respondent's reasons for delay due to depression, marital problems, and young children.
rebuttals.court_answer: Reasons were inconsistent, unsupported, and did not withstand scrutiny; children were adults and no evidence of abandonment by representative.
rebuttals.quote: her reasons do not hold up to scrutiny.

rebuttals.point: Extension of time granted without considering prejudice to Minister.
rebuttals.court_answer: No evidence of prejudice consideration; allowing late appeals risks unfairness and lack of finality.
rebuttals.quote: It does not appear that prejudice to the Minister was considered by the member.

authorities.why: Referenced regarding standard of review for discretionary decisions.
authorities.quote: I should apply a standard of review of reasonableness simpliciter (Callihoo v. Canada)

authorities.authority: Grewal v. Canada (Minister of Employment and Immigration), [1985] 2 F.C. 263 (F.C.A.)
authorities.why: Established criteria for extension of time applications.
authorities.quote: the following criteria must be considered and weighed

authorities.authority: Baksa v. Neis (c.o.b. Brookside Transport), [2002] F.C.J. No. 832
authorities.why: Supported criteria for extension of time applications.
authorities.quote: the following criteria must be considered and weighed

left_open.issue: Appropriate standard of review for extension of time decision
left_open.reason: Court did not need to decide because decision failed on any standard.
left_open.quote: I do not need to reach a conclusion on the appropriate standard since I am satisfied that, on any standard of review, the decision should not stand.
